newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle speed lower late on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle speed lower late on fund selling.

text.p: A late wave of fund selling quickly pushed CME live cattle futures lower, taking feeder cattle futures down as well, analysts and traders said.
Much of the selling was in the December live cattle, where chart-based selling was activated near 66.00 cents per lb and again at 65.75 cents, traders said.
"The bulls are supporting the October, but not the December," said one trader of the break in the latter.
Forecasts for cash cattle trade this week at $72.00 and $73.00 per cwt in feedlot markets impeded declines in the October, they said.
Cash beef prices were lower at ahead of midday but analysts and traders said technical factors rather than the lower beef appeared to be the reason for selling in cattle futures.
At 1217 CDT, live cattle were down 0.800 to 0.150 cent with October off 0.425 at 71.600 cents per lb and December was off 0.800 at 65.400 in active trading.
Feeder cattle were down 0.200 to 0.625 cent with October off 0.200 at 63.300 and November was off 0.625 at 63.800.
